messages:
sam_sales: FYI - BlueHarbor wants to run a 2-week Private deployment POC. Requirements: PrivateLink fronting for control plane, outbound to customer's corporate proxy (with TLS inspection), and certainty that our egress will be a small set of public IPs they can whitelist. They also asked whether we support customer-managed CMKs and FIPS endpoints. Looping in @rachel_platform and @tom_neteng.

rachel_platform: Thanks. Short answers: CMKs: yes for Private deployments. FIPS: we have a FIPS-compatible build available for dedicated stacks; need approval and extra time. For the proxy/tls-inspect flow we recommend mutual TLS from our side to their proxy or a managed NAT with static EIPs on our Dedicated edge.

sam_sales: They said their proxy performs TLS re-encryption (MITM) so domain-only rules won't pass. They need IPs and a firewall snippet. They also want a rough delta vs Hosted API pricing for a 2-week POC.

tom_neteng: Draft firewall snippet (customer egress -> Redwood endpoints):

```
# Example firewall / proxy allowlist
ALLOW TCP 443 TO 34.198.10.11,34.198.10.12  # control-plane ELB EIPs (region us-west-2)
ALLOW TCP 8443 TO 34.198.10.20               # runtime plane EIP (dedicated pool)
DNS: allow outbound to 8.8.8.8 or their internal resolver for our service FQDNs
Note: we'll replace EIPs with the final allocated Elastic IPs per region before kickoff.
```

They must also permit CONNECT to TLS endpoints if using proxy. If using mTLS, we'll provide client certs.

infra_ops: Pricing delta notes: for a 2-week Dedicated POC with static egress we typically bill:
- One-time engineer setup: $1,500
- Dedicated reserved compute (prorated): ~$2,400 (depends on GPU size)
- Static egress IP allocation + NAT appliance (prorated): ~$300
- Estimated egress bandwidth: billed per-GB; estimate 200GB -> $40
We can offer a POC bundle at a flat $3,500 for 14 days to keep it simple. If they go production, monthly commitments apply.

sre-bot: Reminder: Please attach PCI/SOC2 artifacts request to the thread when asked.

sam_sales: BlueHarbor just sent a security questionnaire snippet asking: support for TLS inspection? key rotation cadence? list of public egress IPs? data retention windows? I'll upload the PDF.

rachel_platform: Answers to blueharbor sec-questions (short):
- TLS inspection: supported via proxy/NAT; if they re-sign TLS we need proxy config and cert trust. We recommend mTLS for stronger identity.
- Key rotation: KMS CMKs rotate per their policy; customer-managed CMKs can control rotation schedule.
- Egress IP list: we provide explicit EIPs per-region for Dedicated; we'll publish the final list in the handoff doc.
- Retention: request logs default 90 days, infra traces 30 days; archives available on request.

tom_neteng: Security blockers: if their proxy does active TLS interception they may require our client certs installed in their proxy CA store; also some enterprise IPS appliances block gRPC multiplexing over 8443. If they have that, we can downgrade to plain HTTPS streams but need to know now.

sam_sales: They confirmed TLS interception + corporate proxy with auth. Also asked if our client can do proxy-auth (basic/ntlm).

rachel_platform: We don't support NTLM client auth. We can support proxy with Basic auth headers or run egress NAT so traffic goes out via dedicated EIPs (preferred for fewer proxy headaches).

infra_ops: Action items: 1) tom to produce final EIP list and updated firewall snippet (ETA 24h). 2) rachel to confirm FIPS build availability and CMK instructions (ETA 48h). 3) infra_ops to produce POC flat-price quote doc and SOW template (ETA EOD). 4) sam to upload questionnaire and confirm expected tokens/day.

sre-bot: Meeting scheduled: POC kickoff 2061187200 (calendar invite sent). Assigned owners: sam_sales (owner), rachel_platform (tech lead), tom_neteng (network).

sam_sales: Great 95 I'll push the questionnaire and ask them to pick NAT EIP vs proxy-auth approach. Will update thread with their choice. :+1:
